messages.subject: Re: simple tags, iterators, and conditional iterators in the init statement
messages.subject_clean: simple tags, iterators, and conditional iterators in the init statement
messages.body_plain:
Forgive my multiple messages -- but for those interested -- I checked in with four folks I know who use Mplus Automation and all use regular R code loops for setting iterative conditions prior to creating input files. In either words, they did not have a direct answer to my questions. What I ended up doing was taking the two issues out of the [iters] portion of the file generation and using the DEFINE command within the Mplus portion of the code. Within the DEFINE command I used computations on the iterators for mathematical definitions (issue #1), and the two conditionals on the iterators to create the known variable (issue #2). All is working well now!

Best,
Liz

On Thursday, August 13, 2020 at 8:51:44 AM UTC-7 Elizabeth A. Sanders wrote:
> Also please forgive the extra Rsq on the iterators= line. That's a typo!
>
> On Thursday, August 13, 2020 at 7:49:50 AM UTC-7 Elizabeth A. Sanders wrote:
> > Hello,
> >
> > I am setting up the init section to create a series of Mplus input files and was wondering about these 2 questions:
> >
> > 1) After iterators are defined, can I use a simple tag to define other variables computed from iterator values? Essentially, these 'other' variables become iterators too but I'm not sure how to specify them. For example the resvarY variable below:
> >
> > [[init]]
> > iterators = J m Rsq corXX Rsq;
> > J = 10 30 50;
> > m = 5 10 20;
> > Rsq = .05 .10 .20;
> > corXX = .20 .40;
> > resvarY = 1-Rsq;
> > etc...
> > [[/init]]
> >
> > 2) Is there a way to code conditional loops within the [[init]] code to define a variable that essentially also becomes an iterator? Specifically, I have one variable in particular that has been pre-computed and depends jointly on values of two of my iterators. Something like this:
> >
> > [[init]]
> > iterators = J m Rsq corXX Rsq;
> > J = 10 30 50;
> > m = 5 10 20;
> > Rsq = .05 .10 .20;
> > corXX = .20 .40;
> > resvarY = 1-Rsq;
> > [[Rsq = .05]]
> > [[corrXX = .20]]
> > coeff = valuehere;
> > [[/corrXX = .20]]
> > [[/Rsq = .05]]
> > etc...setting conditionals for all four combinations of corrXX an Rsq...
> > [[/init]]
> >
> > I know the above code does NOT work (I tried it) so any help you can give would be very much appreciated!!
> >
> > Thank you in advance!
> >
> > Best,
> > Liz

messages.subject: LCGA
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone
I'm very new to MPlus. I'm currently writing my Masterthesis for which I'm supposed to use Mplus. And I have to admit, I'm a bit lost here. My Supervisor has only used MPlus together with SPSS. But I don't want to take the detour of exporting everything over.
I got everything installed and mangend to get my R Data File exported into an Mplus inp. file (yeah). But now the row names are just numbered starting with 1 - I do have an ID-variable to identify my cases and I would like to keep this numbering system? I don't want it to get messed up when I'm importing my results back into R....
Which would be my second question: I have to run a LCGA (trying to figure this out right now). Later on I will need the results and class membership back in my R dataframe as I will do some more calculations (regression analysis) with R. How do I get those results back into my original R dataframe? Best would be if there are new variables in my dataframe showing to which class each ID belongs...? Also I cannot read the datafile which I used for the import to Mplus in R anymore - it now always says it's "corrupted"?

I hope it's understandable what my problems are... As I said, I'm feeling a bit lost and my supervisor is always super confident with me, telling me I can figure it out by myself... which I'm trying very hard but deadlines are getting closer. As we never had anything about Mplus or LCGA in my studies, you can imagine how confusing all of this is.

Thanks a Lot! (maybe my problems are not really problems and super simple to solve for you all...)
